sections.h2: Where does a deed get recorded in Columbia County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
The Columbia County Register and Recorder's Office takes it, at 35 West Main Street in Bloomsburg, PA 17815. The phone number is 570-389-5632. The same office handles wills and estates, but a house sale touches only the Recorder of Deeds side.

The office publishes its Recorder of Deeds fee schedule, a realty transfer tax policy and a list of recording requirements on its website. It also points to online access through Landex for searching records. A seller or an agent preparing a closing package should read all three documents, because a deed that breaks one rule is returned for correction.

Bloomsburg, the county seat, is classed as a town rather than a borough, and it is where a courier or a title agent drops off the paperwork for Columbia County closings.

sections.h2: What are the Columbia County recording charges?
sections.html:
A deed or a mortgage costs $87.75 under the schedule that took effect November 17, 2025. Each of those fees already includes a $3.00 Recorder Improvement Fund charge and a $2.00 County Improvement Fund charge, and the amounts marked with two asterisks include the state surcharges added under Act 45.

Columbia County Recorder of Deeds fees, schedule effective November 17, 2025

Extra charges apply on deeds and mortgages only: $1.00 for each name past four, $1.00 for each tract after the first, and $4.00 for each page past four. On every other instrument, those add-ons are 50 cents, 50 cents and $2.00. A veteran's military discharge is recorded free, and the office adds a $2.00 service charge to any document it mails back for corrections.

sections.h2: How many checks does a Columbia County closing need?
sections.html:
Three payments. The county's fee schedule says two separate checks are required for realty transfer tax, each equal to 1 percent of the consideration or fair market value, and the recording fee comes on top of those.

The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue describes the tax as 1 percent state tax on the value of the real estate, collected along with an optional local tax by the county recorder, with buyer and seller jointly liable. The recorder passes the state share to Revenue, and local governments may divide theirs between school districts and municipalities. A deed covering land in more than one municipality must say what percentage of the tax belongs to each.

When the full tax is not being paid, a Statement of Value form takes the place of the check. The county's rules say the form must be completed in full, and any claimed exemption has to be written out on it with the reason. The consideration must read the same in words and in numbers.

sections.h2: What recording requirements does the Columbia County office list?
sections.html:
The county's requirements sheet describes itself as a partial list, and it runs to twenty items. These are the ones that most often decide whether a house deed is accepted.

  • Signatures and initials must be original, and blue ink is preferred.
  • The document must be dated, and the acknowledgment date cannot come before it.
  • The acknowledgment must be a formal one, not "sworn and subscribed," and must include the state, county, date, name, notary signature, stamp and expiration date.
  • A deed must include the buyer's Certificate of Residence or precise address with an original ink signature.
  • A signer who uses a/k/a names must sign each one, and each must appear in the acknowledgment.
  • Foreign language documents need an English translation.
  • The largest page accepted is 8.5 by 14 inches, except for maps, and no margin rules apply because a cover sheet is attached to every document.

Mailed packages must include a stamped, self-addressed envelope big enough for the return. Maps must be signed and acknowledged by the owners; subdivision plans need county or municipal approval and must be recorded within 90 days of it, and the office does not take mylar.

sections.h2: What else does the Columbia County recorder do for a seller?
sections.html:
A name search costs $20.00, plus $0.50 per page for copies, and a certification of Recorder of Deeds documents is $1.50. Copies on 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 paper are $0.50 a page, and 11 by 17 copies are $1.00.

Mistakes can be fixed, but the rules are firm. To re-record a deed, the office wants the original document with its original recording cover sheet, an explanation of why it is being re-recorded, and a new acknowledgment. If the same notary cannot re-acknowledge it, the parties must sign again before a different notary. Mortgage paperwork follows similar address rules: a mortgage must carry the lender's Certificate of Residence or precise address, and an assignment of mortgage must carry the assignee's.

Documents signed by a corporation, partnership or other entity must be executed by an authorized officer, whose title and company name must appear under the signature and again in the acknowledgment.

sections.h2: What is Columbia County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Columbia County was created on March 22, 1813 from part of Northumberland County and covers 483 square miles of land in central Pennsylvania. The Susquehanna River runs through it. Farmland and state game lands cover much of the county, the southern tip belongs to the Coal Region, and part of Ricketts Glen State Park lies in the north. Fishing Creek, Briar Creek, Catawissa Creek and Roaring Creek are the other main streams.

Bloomsburg had 14,855 residents in 2010 and Berwick 10,477, which makes them the two population centers. Catawissa, Millville, Benton and Orangeville are smaller boroughs. Centralia, the tiniest, had 10 residents in the 2010 census. The Census Bureau estimated 66,193 people in July 2025, up 2.3 percent from the 2020 base, and it is the only one of these four counties that gained residents.

sections.h2: What should a Columbia County seller prepare?
sections.html:
Start with the title company or attorney handling the closing, and ask who will deliver the deed to Main Street in Bloomsburg.

  • Confirm the November 17, 2025 fee total for the deed's page and name count.
  • Draw two transfer tax checks of 1 percent each, plus the recording fee check.
  • Check that the notary block names the right county and carries an unexpired commission.
  • Add the buyer's Certificate of Residence, signed in ink.
  • Include a self-addressed stamped envelope if the package goes by mail.

Owners of inherited houses should find out whether the transfer is exempt; the Department of Revenue exempts property passing by will or intestate succession, and the county requires a Statement of Value to document any exemption.

faqs.q: What is Columbia County's base charge for a deed?
faqs.a: The fee is $87.75 for a deed or mortgage under the schedule effective November 17, 2025. Names, tracts and pages beyond the limits add $1.00, $1.00 and $4.00 each on deeds and mortgages.

faqs.q: Does Columbia County want one check or several?
faqs.a: Two, each for 1 percent of the consideration or fair market value, plus a separate check for the recording fee. The county's fee schedule states that two separate checks are required.

faqs.q: Does Columbia County require a Certificate of Residence on a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Every deed must carry the buyer's Certificate of Residence or precise address, signed with an original ink signature.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Columbia County recorder?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the package meets every recording requirement and includes a stamped, self-addressed envelope large enough for the return. The office is at 35 West Main Street, Bloomsburg, and its phone is 570-389-5632.

faqs.q: How soon must a Columbia County subdivision plan be recorded?
faqs.a: A subdivision map or land development plan must be recorded within 90 days of its approval date. It needs approval from the county or the municipality, and the office does not accept mylar.
